budget_tax_bill_mod_browser_link: Not sure what you're legally insured on? Look up the minimum for your activity →
mod_browser_desc: What is the legal minimum your employer must insure you on? Прил. 1/1А ЗБДОО sets it per economic activity and occupational group — and it rose for most of them on 1 August 2026.
mod_browser_intro: 86 economic activities (КИД-2025) × 9 occupational qualification groups. Search by name or by КИД code.
mod_browser_search: Search by activity or КИД code
mod_browser_tzpb: Work-injury contribution (ТЗПБ, Прил. 2/2А): {{before}}% until 31 July, {{after}}% from 1 August. Paid by the employer, on top of the amounts above.
budget_tax_bill_civil_servant_note: КСО art. 4(1) items 2, 3 and 10 — state civil servants, judges, prosecutors and investigators. Until 1 August 2026 the budget paid both contribution shares for them; § 6 ЗБДОО, § 5 (universal pension fund 4/1 for Aug–Dec) and § 20 ЗБНЗОК phase them onto an employer/employee split (pension 11.8/3.0, then 8.22/6.58 from 1 January 2027; health 80:20). The total burden does not change — 32.30% throughout — only who remits it. The figures below show the deduction itself; the law's intent is that pay rises absorb it, which this calculator does not assume. This does NOT change contributions for ordinary employment contracts (item 1); defence and security (item 4) are explicitly kept on the old regime. ТЗПБ is excluded — it is set per economic activity.
budget_tax_bill_mod_default_stepped: default for {{year}} — in force from {{from}} (was {{prev}} before)
budget_tax_bill_mod_reset_stepped: reset to the {{year}} default {{eur}} €, in force from {{from}} (was {{prev}})
budget_tax_bill_above_cap_hint: Above the МОД cap each extra euro is taxed at only 10% — the effective rate falls as the salary rises.
budget_tax_bill_include_employer: Include employer contributions in the breakdown below
budget_tax_bill_vat_note: 20% VAT embedded in everyday spending, assuming {{pct}} of net income goes to standard-rated goods.
budget_tax_bill_pension_into: Paid into the pension system: {{total}}{{per}} (you {{you}} + employer {{employer}}).
budget_tax_bill_pension_into_self: Paid into the pension system: {{total}}{{per}} (you remit the full amount).
budget_tax_bill_pension_ages: Retirement in 2026: women at 62y 6m (36y 10m of service), men at 64y 9m (39y 10m of service).
budget_tax_bill_pension_caption: Simplified: pension ≈ insurable income × 1.35% × years of service, bounded by the 2026 minimum (€322) and maximum (€1,738) pension. The real formula weighs lifetime earnings against the national average.
budget_tax_bill_caption: Approximate estimate. Assumes a default-case taxpayer (born after 1959, no second-pillar opt-out). SSC stops accruing above the МОД; above the cap only the 10% income tax keeps scaling. Social-security contributions are earmarked (pension + health + unemployment), not freely allocable — the breakdown applies general-government spending shares to the whole bill purely for illustration.
budget_tax_bill_company_caption: Simplified: 10% corporate tax on profit, then 5% tax when the remainder is distributed as a dividend. Corporate tax is assessed annually; the owner's own social-security contributions are not modelled here.
budget_tax_bill_curve_title: Effective rate across the salary range
budget_tax_bill_curve_caption: Effective tax-and-contribution rate by gross salary. Once salary passes the МОД cap social security stops growing and the rate falls — the burden turns regressive at the top.
budget_tax_bill_tip_ssc: Employee social-security and health contributions — pension 8.78%, health 3.20%, sickness/maternity 1.40%, unemployment 0.40%. Charged on insurable income up to the МОД cap.
budget_tax_bill_tip_mod: Maximum insurable income (МОД) — the monthly ceiling above which no further social-security contributions are due. Income tax still applies to the whole salary.
budget_tax_bill_tip_rate: Effective rate = total tax and contributions ÷ gross income. Marginal rate = the tax on the next euro earned; it falls to 10% above the МОД cap, where social security stops.
budget_tax_bill_tip_wedge: Tax wedge — the share of the full cost of employing you (gross salary plus employer contributions) taken by tax and social security rather than reaching your take-home pay.
budget_tax_calculator_page_description: Estimate your income tax, social-security contributions and VAT for an employee, self-employed person or company owner — and see which government functions your tax bill funds.
budget_tax_calculator_page_intro: Pick a taxpayer profile and income to see your monthly tax and social-security bill, the VAT embedded in your spending, and how it maps onto general-government spending — plus a projection of your future pension.

budget_citizen_policy_sim_link: What if a tax rate changes? Open the budget simulator
budget_policy_page_description: What happens to Bulgaria's budget balance if taxes (VAT, the flat income tax, corporate, dividends, the МОД cap, excise) or spending (pensions, wages, social benefits, subsidies) change? Move a slider and see the dynamic estimate (behavioral response + uncertainty band) — and the effect on a worked payslip.
budget_policy_page_intro: Move a slider and see two numbers at once: the change in the consolidated budget balance per year, and the change on one worked payslip per month. The default estimate is dynamic — with behavioral response and an uncertainty band; static mode (fixed base, no response) is one tap away.

budget_policy_error: The policy baseline data could not be loaded — please try again later.
budget_policy_tip_vat_std: Applies to every consumption category not assigned to the reduced or zero rate. Current law: 20%.
budget_policy_tip_vat_red: The level of the reduced rate. Current law: 9%, applied to hotel accommodation, books and periodicals, baby goods.
budget_policy_tip_groups: Assign a consumption category to the standard, reduced or zero rate. Defaults reflect current law after the temporary pandemic-era cuts expired at end-2024.
budget_policy_tip_pit: The 10% flat tax on employment and other personal income. The final-tax portion (dividends to individuals, non-residents) keeps its own rate and is not rescaled.
budget_policy_tip_div: The 5% withholding on distributed dividends. Scored on the corporate-withholding budget line; dividends taxed inside personal income tax are not rescaled.
budget_policy_tip_excise: Each excise is the actual rate in its real unit, with a "like in…" EU-country quick-select (press the (i)). BG fuel sits at the EU floor; wine is a new excise on today's zero rate. Over €3.8B a year in total — more than corporate tax.
budget_policy_tip_excise_diesel: Specific excise on diesel (~€1.03B in 2025). Bulgaria sits at the EU floor, so there is no legal room to cut. Current law: €330/1000 L.
budget_policy_tip_excise_petrol: Specific excise on unleaded petrol (~€0.30B in 2025). Current law: €363/1000 L — just above the EU floor of €359.
budget_policy_tip_excise_cigarettes: Total cigarette excise (specific + a share of the price); scales the whole tobacco line (~€2.15B in 2025). The EU floor is €90/1000 and ≥60% of price. Current law: ~€114/1000. A large hike pushes sales to the illicit and cross-border market — so a steep rise can even lower revenue.
budget_policy_tip_excise_spirits: Excise on ethyl alcohol — rakia, spirits (the bulk of the ~€177M alcohol excise in 2025). The EU floor is €550/hl of pure alcohol. Current law: €562/hl. Some demand shifts to home production (the still).
budget_policy_tip_excise_wine: Bulgaria taxes wine at €0 — as does the EU minimum, so introducing one is a legal choice. The commercial market (~940,000 hl) is taxed; much home-made wine stays untaxed.
budget_policy_gambling: Gambling — fee on gross gaming revenue (GGR)
budget_policy_tip_gambling: The Gambling Act variable fee on gross gaming revenue (stakes minus payouts) for betting/lottery/online. Raised from 20% to 25% in 2026. The base (GGR ~€716M in 2025) is НАП/industry-reported — NOT a standalone budget line (gambling is an alternative tax folded into 'Corporate tax'/'Other taxes' + fees). A high rate pushes play to unlicensed/offshore operators — so a big hike can even shrink revenue. EU regimes vary widely (some tax GGR at 15–25%+, others turnover), so there is no direct 'like in…' country pick.
budget_policy_tip_vignettes: A % increase on e-vignettes only (cars ≤3.5t; base ≈€180M/year, АПИ). Near-inelastic — you must hold a vignette to drive. The 2026 framework proposed +30% (≈€53M). For readability we show the ANNUAL vignette price (official tariff BGN 97 ≈ €49.60; resellers add a fee on top); the uplift applies equally to every duration — daily, weekend, weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual.
budget_policy_tip_tolls: A % increase on the per-km toll only (trucks/buses; base ≈€380M/year, АПИ). At higher rates heavy transit can divert through neighbouring countries.
budget_policy_tip_soe: A % cut of the state-enterprise subsidy envelope (БДЖ, НКЖИ, Bulgarian Post; ≈€316M). Caveat: much is locked in multi-year public-service / infrastructure contracts, so a real operating cut near the ceiling isn't feasible — the draft budget books €285M (≈90%), but most of that is avoided indexation, not a real cut. The figure here is face value; our independent re-pricing assumes ≈35% realisation (15–55%), i.e. for a 90% cut only ≈€100M of ≈€284M is realistically bankable.
budget_policy_tip_mod: Максимален осигурителен доход — the monthly ceiling on insurable income. Raising it collects contributions on wages above the cap; lowering it forfeits them. Both directions are scored over the fitted earnings distribution, including the income-tax offset (a bigger insurable base means more deducted contributions).
budget_policy_tip_nm: Tax-free amount of the monthly taxable base (income after social-security contributions). The recurring proposal sets it at the minimum wage. Applied to employment income via the earnings distribution.
budget_policy_tip_social: Change to social spending excluding pensions (≈€4B: social & personal assistance, child & disability benefits, unemployment). One of the two main Budget-2026 deficit drivers (alongside public-sector wages). Base: COFOG social protection €15.1B minus pensions €11.1B.
budget_policy_social_compare: Total social protection: BG {{bg}}% of GDP · EU avg {{eu}}%.
budget_policy_tip_interest: Change to debt-interest spending (≈€0.7B, КФП Interest line). Rises as new debt accumulates — Budget 2026 lifts the debt to 30.1% of GDP.
budget_policy_tip_subsidies: Change to general subsidies (≈€1.0B: agriculture, energy, etc.). The БДЖ/НКЖИ/Post transport subsidies are the separate lever above.
budget_policy_preset_budget2026_tip: Loads only the CONSOLIDATION MEASURES from the draft Budget 2026 (МОД cap €2,300, vignettes +30%, an SOE-subsidy cut, the accelerated cigarette excise) — these IMPROVE the balance. IMPORTANT: the budget's actual deficit is −5.7% of GDP (€7.2B) — the highest in years — because spending (public-sector wages + social payments) grows far more than these measures save. This lever shows only the savings; use the Social benefits, Interest and wage levers to explore the spending side.
budget_policy_preset_nm_mrz_tip: The recurring trade-union proposal: no income tax on the first €620 of the monthly taxable base.
budget_policy_preset_progressive_tip: A second 20% rate on the part of the taxable base above €2,000/month, 10% below.
budget_policy_preset_food9_tip: Move food to the reduced VAT rate — the most often proposed VAT change.
budget_policy_preset_restaurants9_tip: Restore the reduced rate for restaurants and catering that expired at end-2024.
budget_policy_preset_nocap_tip: Remove the МОД ceiling so contributions apply to the full wage.
budget_policy_preset_cpionly_tip: Index pensions by inflation only instead of the 50/50 Swiss rule.
budget_policy_preset_admin10_tip: Cut a tenth of administration positions — vacancies absorb most of it.
budget_policy_preset_ssp_tip: Under КСО art. 6(5) the budget still pays both contribution shares for ≈69k people in defence and security (item 4); the lever moves the standard employee share (13.78%) onto them, uncompensated. Civil servants and the judiciary (items 2, 3 and 10) were already moved by § 6 ЗБДОО-2026 and are not counted here.
budget_policy_preset_maternity1_tip: Drop the paid second year of maternity leave (€398.81/mo) — floated by a ПБ MP on 1 June 2026; the party officially disavowed it the same day.
budget_policy_proj_macro: Assumptions for {{year}}: GDP {{gdp}}, real growth {{growth}}%, inflation {{hicp}}%, unemployment {{unemp}}% (EC Spring 2026 forecast).
budget_policy_comparator: The total change equals {{health}}% of annual general-government health spending, or {{education}}% of education spending ({{year}}).
budget_policy_sentence: Scenario: {{changes}} — effect {{total}}/yr on the budget balance ({{pct}}% of GDP).
budget_policy_incidence_caption: Net monthly effect (pay + VAT on spending) by gross salary, employee profile.
budget_policy_tip_exp: Spending levers from the budget debate. Their effects flow into the same headline as the tax levers — as the impact on the budget balance.
budget_policy_tip_swiss: The Swiss rule indexes pensions each July by 50% inflation + 50% insurable-income growth. Shift the weight: 100% = CPI-only (cheaper while wages outgrow prices), 0% = income-only.
budget_policy_nosupp: Do not index the COVID supplement
budget_policy_tip_nosupp: The 60 лв supplement folded into pension bases in July 2022. Excluding that slice from indexation trims each round's cost.
budget_policy_tip_admin: Share of administration positions eliminated. Vacant positions absorb cuts first and save almost nothing; real layoffs also return part of the saving as lost income tax and contributions.
budget_policy_tip_mrz: Кодекс на труда чл. 244 pegs next year's МРЗ to 50% of the average gross wage. Freezing it cuts the budget two ways: it forgoes the contributions + income tax on the private wages the formula would have lifted (a loss), but avoids the payroll the budget itself pays its own low-wage staff (≈{{share}}% of the affected wage mass — a saving). The row shows the net; freezing turns net-positive only above ~31% public share.
budget_policy_mrz_note: Private SSC + tax forgone {{loss}}; public payroll avoided {{save}}
budget_policy_admin_note: ({{vac}}% of the cut falls on vacant positions)
budget_policy_tip_def: Target defense spending as % of GDP under the NATO definition (currently ~2.2%; differs from the national-accounts COFOG figure by military pensions and equipment timing). Priced against the projected GDP.
budget_policy_tip_wi: Indexes the consolidated personnel bill (wages + contributions, €6.3B executed). The 2026 draft proposed +5% with exempted sectors.
budget_policy_wex: Exempt военни, полицаи, лекари, учители (≈55% of the bill)
budget_policy_tip_kap: Changes PLANNED capital expenditure; the cash effect is scaled by the historical execution rate ({{rate}}%) — plans that would not have been executed cost or save nothing when changed on paper.
budget_policy_ssp: Civil servants pay their own contributions
budget_policy_tip_ssp: § 6 ЗБДОО-2026 narrowed КСО art. 6(5) to item 4 alone, so from 1 August 2026 civil servants, judges, prosecutors and investigators already pay their own share — that is enacted law, not a policy choice. What remains is ≈69k people in defence and security (military, МВР, the special services), for whom the budget still pays both shares. The lever moves the standard employee share (13.78%) onto them; the elevated special-category rates stay budget-paid. Uncompensated, the saving is the employee share minus the income tax that falls with it; realistic reforms compensate with higher pay.
budget_policy_tip_hp: Percentage points added to the 8% health-insurance contribution, collected on the employee insurable base (€31.5B).
budget_policy_tip_mp: Pensions below the minimum are topped up to it. Raising the minimum pension costs the top-up to the new floor for every pensioner below it — over НОИ's distribution of pensioners by basic monthly pension size.
budget_policy_tip_tp: The "125% of the average wage" policy pegs teachers' pay to the economy-wide average. The current ratio uses the public-education sector average wage as a proxy — it includes non-teaching staff too. The cost includes employer contributions.
budget_policy_frag_ssp_gross: civil servants pay own contributions (grossed up)
budget_policy_frag_tp: teachers' pay at {{v}}% of the average wage
budget_policy_tip_mat: The child-raising benefit for ages 1–2 is €398.81/mo (frozen by the extension law); the program cost €154M in 2025 (НОИ). Cutting it from 2 years to 1 was floated by a ПБ MP on 1 June 2026; the party officially disavowed it the same day — here you can price it. Dynamic mode adds the income tax + contributions of the mothers who return to work earlier (central 45%, a recapture on top of the saving; the 50%-if-working rule informs the band); static mode ignores it.
budget_policy_tip_mpf: The base salary is 3× the public-sector average wage (€4,236 since May 2026), recalculated quarterly; on 11 June 2026 the legal committee approved the freeze unanimously. The saving is one year of foregone growth on the pay mass of 240 MPs with extras; the president, PM and ministers ride the same base and would add a small extra saving, not modeled.
budget_policy_tip_psub: Since 30 April 2026 the subsidy is €3.00 per valid vote (cut from €4.09 = 8 лв, adopted 3 June 2026). Ten formations cleared the 1% bar on 19 April 2026 — 3.10M subsidized votes ≈ €9.3M in a full year. The €8.96M in the 2026 budget is not a full-year figure: that year straddles both the rate change and the election that reset the vote base.
budget_policy_tip_corp: A single 10% rate on profits (since 2007). Static scaling of corporate receipts; ignores profit shifting and behavioral response.
budget_policy_discuss: Discuss your scenario in the Наясно group
budget_policy_affect_nm: Touches {{pct}} of employees — monthly taxable base below the threshold.
budget_policy_affect_b2: The second rate touches {{pct}} of employees.
budget_policy_affect_mod: Touches {{pct}} of employees — wages above the cap.
budget_policy_affect_mat: The second year is used by ≈ {{n}} mothers a year.
budget_policy_affect_mp: ≈ {{n}} pensioners get topped up to the new minimum.
budget_policy_affect_ssp: Affects ≈ {{n}} people — defence and security. Civil servants and the judiciary already moved to a split under § 6 ЗБДОО-2026, so they are not counted here.

budget_policy_public_submit_tip: Sends your lever settings (no personal data) to the simulator's public statistics. Once per scenario.
budget_policy_public_edp: {{pct}}% of scenarios bring the deficit under 3% of GDP
budget_policy_public_few: Not enough scenarios for statistics yet — add yours.
budget_policy_public_dev_blocked: Submitting is disabled in dev mode (the proxy points at production).
budget_policy_public_caption: Voluntarily submitted scenarios; the figures (effect, median, shares) are computed in each visitor's own browser and are not centrally verified. Not a representative sample. No personal data is stored.
budget_policy_tip_mode_static: Static scoring: bases held fixed, no behavioral response — the convention of official costings.
budget_policy_tip_mode_dynamic: Dynamic scoring: adds behavioral base responses (reporting, shifting, compliance), a macro feedback on GDP and a 90% uncertainty band.
budget_policy_goal_edp_tip: Bring the deficit under 3% of GDP — the threshold behind the EC's excessive-deficit-procedure recommendation (2026-06-03).
budget_policy_goal_edp_desc: Deficit under 3% of GDP in {{year}} — close the excessive-deficit gap
budget_policy_goal_debt_tip: Keep government debt under 40% of GDP at the end of the projection. The baseline drifts to ~43%.
budget_policy_goal_debt_desc: Government debt under 40% of GDP in {{year}}
budget_policy_goal_def_tip: Reach 3% of GDP on defense (NATO definition) without a first-year deficit worse than the baseline.
budget_policy_goal_def_desc: Defense at 3% of GDP without worsening the {{year}} balance vs the baseline
budget_policy_goal_def_note: The defense lever sits at {{v}}% of GDP — the mission needs ≥ 3.0% and a balance no worse than the baseline.
budget_policy_decile_title: Who gains, who loses — by employee decile
budget_policy_decile_caption: Mean monthly change (net pay + VAT on spending) for each tenth of wage earners ordered by gross salary — employees only, over a wage distribution validated against the 2023 НАП data.
budget_policy_tip_total: Static estimate against the {{year}} executed budget: bases held fixed, only rates and rules change. Positive = the balance improves.
budget_policy_hero_range: {{low}} … {{high}} — 9 in 10 simulations fall within this band
budget_policy_tip_total_dyn: Dynamic estimate against the {{year}} executed budget: the static effect plus behavioral base responses and a year-1 GDP feedback. Positive = the balance improves.
budget_policy_tip_deficit: The consolidated cash deficit for {{year}}, after your levers. The baseline is the EC spring forecast (−4.1% of GDP); the government's own draft budget projects a higher deficit — about −5.7% of GDP (≈ −€7.2B). The sliders show how the measures move the balance against the baseline.
budget_policy_tip_excise_tobacco_row: The dynamic estimate accounts for illicit and cross-border substitution — on a steep hike the revenue can land well below the static figure.
budget_policy_tip_gambling_row: The dynamic estimate accounts for migration to unlicensed/offshore operators — at high rates the revenue can land well below the static figure.
budget_policy_tip_road_charges_row: The dynamic estimate nets out heavy-vehicle cross-border diversion and the collection ramp on the uplift — small, since car vignettes barely respond.
budget_policy_tip_soe_row: The face-value budget effect of cutting BDZh/NRIC/Post subsidies. Real feasibility is lower — much is locked in public-service and infrastructure contracts.
budget_policy_tip_mod_row: Includes the income-tax interaction: a different cap changes the contributions deducted from the taxable base.
budget_policy_no_change: Current law — move a slider to score a scenario.
budget_policy_baseline_note: Baseline: {{year}} executed revenue — VAT {{vat}}, personal income tax {{pit}}. Sources: КФП monthly execution, НАП annual report, Eurostat national accounts.
budget_policy_citizen_caption: Employee profile, no child relief, 75% of net spent on VAT-carrying consumption. The full per-person breakdown lives in the tax calculator.
budget_top_deviations_subtitle: Spending units whose execution diverged most from the original budget law, fiscal year
budget_top_deviations_caption: Plan = the appropriation as originally voted (ЗДБРБ). Executed = the annual execution report. These are the top five by PERCENTAGE deviation, limited to units with a plan above €20M. The full list is ordered by absolute difference in euro and therefore reads in a different order.
budget_journey_subtitle: Law → execution → audit, per fiscal year.
budget_methodology_description: Where the budget data comes from, how it is processed, and what the dashboard covers.
budget_meth_source_p: The figures come from the Ministry of Finance dataset “state budget execution by major budget indicators”, published on the national open-data portal data.egov.bg under a public-domain (CC0) licence. The Ministry publishes one resource per monthly cash-execution snapshot; each lists, for the five top-level sections of the state budget, the amount set by the budget law and the amount executed so far that fiscal year.
budget_meth_sections_p: The Bulgarian state budget execution table has five top-level sections, and the dashboard tracks each of them over time:
budget_meth_revenue: — tax and non-tax revenue, grants and donations.
budget_meth_expenditure: — spending and transfers: personnel, operations, capital, social spending, subsidies, interest.
budget_meth_eu: — Bulgaria's contribution to the common EU budget.
budget_meth_balance: — revenue minus expenditure minus the EU contribution. Negative means a deficit.
budget_meth_financing: — how the balance is financed: external and domestic borrowing, deposits, privatisation.
budget_meth_currency_p: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026. Monthly snapshots up to and including December 2025 are published in leva; from January 2026 they are in euro. Every figure on the dashboard is shown in euro.
budget_meth_cumulative_p: Each monthly snapshot is cumulative year-to-date: the December figure is the whole year, and the series resets each January. The execution-trend chart shows this directly — a ramp within each fiscal year, then a reset.
budget_meth_integrity_p: The ingest fails loudly rather than publish partial data: a pinned snapshot is re-parsed on every run and byte-compared against a committed fixture, so any drift in the parser is caught before anything is written, and a change touching more than a small fraction of the data aborts the run for review.
budget_meth_ministries_p: Each first-level spending unit (ministry, agency, independent body) publishes its own annual execution report. The ingest parses these PDFs into a uniform admin-grain table and reconciles them against the State Budget Law, so each ministry page shows planned versus actual at the ministry level and one column deeper at the program level.
budget_meth_documents_p: Each fiscal year is linked to its source documents — the State Budget Law as promulgated in Държавен вестник, the mid-year amendment laws, the year-end execution report, and the report of the National Audit Office. The fiscal-year page surfaces the timeline and the original links.
budget_meth_procurement_p: Each spending unit's page links to the public-procurement contracts it awarded under the Public Procurement Act, so a budget line can be followed all the way down to the individual contracts that consumed it.
budget_projection_pending: full-year projection pending — needs a prior fiscal year for the seasonal baseline
budget_term_no_data: No budget data for this parliament’s term yet.
budget_ministries_subtitle: Expenditure appropriated by the State Budget Law for fiscal year
budget_ministry_not_found: No budget-law data found for this spending unit.
budget_ministry_intro: Appropriations set by the State Budget Law. Ministry-level execution (actual spending) is published in the year-end execution report and is not yet ingested.
budget_ministry_intro_with_execution: Appropriations from the State Budget Law plus actual execution from the year-end program-budget report (Отчет за изпълнението на програмния бюджет).
budget_ministry_procurement_mp: MP-connected contractor(s) paid by this unit
budget_ministry_trend_subtitle_with_exec: Planned appropriations (State Budget Law) and actual execution per fiscal year.
budget_ministry_trend_subtitle_planned_o: Planned appropriations (State Budget Law) per fiscal year. Execution is published in the year-end report and is not yet ingested for this unit.
budget_fy_status_law_only_long: law plan only — no monthly execution feed for this year yet
budget_explorer_description: Travel public spending one level at a time — by spending unit within the state budget, or by function across the whole general-government sector.
budget_explorer_caption_admin: First-level spending units in the State Budget Law (Ministry of Finance). Amounts are as appropriated; open a unit to see its programmes.
budget_explorer_caption_functional: Expenditure by function (COFOG) comes from Eurostat and covers the whole general-government sector — the state together with municipalities and the social security funds. It is not a breakdown of the state budget.
budget_explorer_empty: No data for this dimension and year.
budget_explorer_empty_coverage: This dimension only goes up to {{year}}.
budget_units_description: Every first-level spending unit in the State Budget Law — what each was appropriated, and which reported execution.
budget_units_intro: These are the first-level spending units named in the State Budget Law — not only ministries: the President's Administration, the State Fund for Agriculture, ДАНС, КЕВР and others are here too.
budget_units_coverage: {{covered}} of {{total}} spending units published an execution report. The rest have only a plan — the gap is theirs, not ours.
budget_units_pending: Execution reports for {{fy}} are published after the fiscal year closes — so far this is the plan only.
budget_units_empty: No spending units for this year or search.
budget_units_source: Source: the State Budget Law and the annual programme-budget execution reports (Ministry of Finance).
budget_units_shared_eik: the same body is listed under its other name too — do not add them up
budget_units_no_contracts: no contracts recorded in this year
budget_revenue_description: State budget revenue by source — taxes, social contributions, grants and the rest.
budget_revenue_intro: The state lives mainly on taxes. These are the state budget's revenues for the selected year, broken down by source exactly as the Ministry of Finance reports them.
budget_revenue_source: Source: Ministry of Finance — state budget execution by major budget indicators (data.egov.bg). The EU comparison is Eurostat.
budget_comp_trend_h: How it changes over the years
budget_comp_cumulative_note: Each year is shown at its latest reported period — КФП figures accumulate from the start of the year, so adding the months would count them many times over.
budget_comp_eu_h: How Bulgaria compares in the EU
budget_comp_eu_body: {{bg}}% of GDP against an EU average of {{eu}}% — №{{rank}} of {{total}} ({{year}}).
budget_comp_partial_mix: This is the split as of {{period}} — the year's structure is still moving, so each share is provisional.
budget_spending_description: State budget expenditure by type — for the selected year, over time and against the EU.
budget_spending_intro: State budget expenditure by type, as reported by the Ministry of Finance. A large share of it is not spent by the state budget itself but passed on to the pension and health funds, municipalities, state universities, the Academy of Sciences and the public broadcasters, which spend it — that is the “Трансфери (нето)” line, meaning transfers made minus transfers received back. Bulgaria's contribution to the EU budget (roughly €0.8–1.0bn a year) is a separate section of the report and is not included in the total here.
budget_spending_source: Source: Ministry of Finance, cash execution of the consolidated fiscal programme (КФП), via data.egov.bg. The EU comparison is from Eurostat (gov_10a_main).
budget_dev_title: Plan versus outturn, by spending unit
budget_dev_description: What parliament voted each spending unit, how the plan was amended, and what was actually spent.
budget_dev_intro: The budget act sets a ceiling for every first-level spending unit. These are the three figures that track it: the plan as voted, the adjusted plan at year end, and the execution report. Keeping them apart matters — “spent more than the act allowed” and “the ceiling was raised during the year” are different findings, and a single “deviation” column merges them.
budget_dev_coverage: {{covered}} of {{total}} spending units published an execution report for {{fy}}.
budget_dev_coverage_note: The ranking below can only show those. The rest have a plan and no report — that absence belongs to the body concerned, not to the data here.
budget_dev_coverage_none: The year has closed and not one spending unit has published a report — that is a finding, not an empty table. The plan is known; the execution is not.
budget_dev_delta_note: “Δ vs the act” compares the outturn with the budget as originally voted; “Δ vs the adjusted plan” with the ceiling in force at year end. A wide gap between the two means the ceiling moved during the year, not that the body overspent. The adjusted plan folds in every change — an amending act, a Council of Ministers decree, or internal compensated reallocation — and the source does not tell them apart, so no claim is made here about who raised it.
budget_dev_delta_note_no_amendments: The source publishes no adjusted plan by spending unit for this year, so there is only one difference to show — against the act as voted.
budget_dev_source: Source: Ministry of Finance — the state budget act, the adjusted plan and per-unit execution reports, via data.egov.bg.
budget_dev_see_all: All spending units, by absolute difference
budget_dev_coverage_pending: The year is still running, so execution reports are not yet due. What is missing here is the calendar, not silence.
budget_law_description: Which of the documents used to judge whether a budget is public exist for Bulgaria — and what was published for each year.
budget_law_intro: The international standard (Open Budget Survey) names eight documents that together make a budget traceable — from the framework before it is tabled to the independent audit after it closes. This is which of them are collected on this site, and what exactly was published for the selected year.
budget_law_frame_score: {{covered}} of {{total}} are collected on this site.
budget_law_frame_caveat: This is coverage HERE, not a score for the country. A document that is not ticked may well exist and simply not be collected in this database — the site mainly gathers what is published as open data. For an international assessment of Bulgaria, see the Open Budget Survey.
budget_law_year_empty: No documents are collected for this year.
budget_law_year_note: The ticks above cover the whole site while this list is one year, so the two do not match. The monthly КФП reports, for instance, are not filed against a particular year and appear in no year's list.
budget_law_coverage_running: {{months}} monthly snapshots, the year has not closed
budget_law_source: Source: the Ministry of Finance and the National Audit Office — acts, amendments, execution reports and audit reports, via data.egov.bg and the bodies' own sites.
budget_exec_description: The plan in the act against the cash outturn for the whole year — revenue, expenditure, the EU contribution and the balance they produce.
budget_exec_intro: A budget act is a forecast. This page shows what actually happened: how much was collected, how much was spent and what balance came out — with the difference from plan on every line.
budget_exec_identity: The balance is not a separate figure: it is revenue minus expenditure minus the EU contribution. That is why the contribution sits on its own line — added into expenditure it would produce a total the Ministry of Finance publishes nowhere.
budget_exec_identity_broken: For this year the lines do not sum to the published balance, so no claim is made here that one follows from the other.
budget_exec_financing_note: Financing for the year is {{amount}} — the balance with its sign flipped, not a second quantity: a deficit and the financing of it are one thing seen from either side.
budget_exec_gdp_h: The balance as a share of GDP
budget_exec_gdp_note: Against GDP of {{gdp}} for the year.
budget_exec_eu_body: On Eurostat's basis Bulgaria is at {{bg}}% of GDP against an EU average of {{eu}}% — №{{rank}} of {{total}} ({{year}}).
budget_exec_partial: The year has not closed. The outturn is as of {{asOf}}.
budget_exec_empty: No outturn data for this year.
budget_exec_source: Source: Ministry of Finance, cash execution of the consolidated fiscal programme (КФП), via data.egov.bg. The EU comparison is from Eurostat (gov_10a_main).
budget_exec_see_all: Plan against outturn for the whole year
budget_exec_gdp_note_projected: Projected for the full year, against GDP of {{gdp}}. The outturn so far covers part of the year and is not divided by a full-year GDP — that would halve the figure.
budget_exec_partial_projection: The year has not closed — the outturn is as of {{asOf}}. It has no full appropriation voted in an act, so the comparison is against the projection for the whole year.
budget_func_title: What the money goes on — by function
budget_func_description: General-government spending by function: social protection, health, education, defence and the rest, on Eurostat's basis.
budget_func_intro: Here spending is grouped by WHAT IT IS FOR rather than by who spends it. The classification is COFOG — the international standard countries are compared on.
budget_func_perimeter: Note: this is the WHOLE general-government sector — the state, municipalities and the social funds, consolidated: {{total}} for the year. The other pages in this section show the state budget alone, which is considerably smaller. The two totals neither add up nor contradict each other: the perimeter differs, and so does the method — this is accrual on the European basis, that is cash execution.
budget_func_not_ministries: A function is not a body. „Health“ covers all health spending at every level of government — state, municipalities and the health fund — not the Ministry of Health's budget.
budget_func_empty: No functional breakdown for this year.
budget_func_empty_coverage: Eurostat's functional data runs to {{year}}; later years are not published yet.
budget_staff_title: How many people the administration employs
budget_staff_description: Budgeted posts in the state administration — approved, filled and vacant — over time, from the annual report on the state of the administration.
budget_staff_intro: Every year the government reports how many posts the administration has, how many are filled and how many stand empty. These are those figures over time.
budget_staff_vacancy_rate: Vacancies are {{pct}}% of the establishment in {{fy}} — the share the report itself publishes, not a difference between two different sources.
budget_staff_nsi_h: The NSI figure (employees on the payroll)
budget_staff_nsi_note: The same report also contains a separate NSI table of employees on the payroll at December. It does NOT include the interior and defence ministries, but it does include people engaged outside the approved establishment — under Council of Ministers decrees 66/1996 and 212/1993 and employment programmes. Neither figure is therefore a subset of the other, and the report itself states the two are not comparable. They are not subtracted: vacant posts are a separate number, published directly.
budget_staff_source: Source: the annual report on the state of the administration (Council of Ministers). That report publishes no payroll — the amounts in the ranking above come from the ministries' own programme-budget reports and are on a different basis.
budget_inv_description: The projects the budget act appropriates capital funds for — by type and by province.
budget_inv_intro: Each budget act comes with a named list of the projects capital funds are set aside for: roads, schools, water, hospitals. This is that list, summarised by type and by province.
budget_inv_plan_warning: This is a PLAN, not an outturn. The list shows what the act set money aside for, not what was built, started or paid. Per-project execution is not published in this form, which is why there is no „outturn“ column here.
budget_inv_top_note: This is a leaderboard, not the whole list — the rows below sum to only part of the total.
budget_inv_source: Source: Annex III to the State Budget Act, as promulgated in the State Gazette.
budget_funds_description: Revenue, spending and balance of the pension fund, the teachers' pension fund and the guaranteed-claims fund — and how much of it the state budget covers.
budget_funds_intro: Pensions and benefits are paid by the social-security funds, not directly from the state budget. The largest of them — the state social security fund — does not live on its own revenue, and the difference arrives as a transfer from the budget; the smaller ones cover themselves. This is that account, fund by fund.
budget_funds_self: The fund's own revenue covers {{pct}}% of its spending.
budget_funds_identity: The balance is not revenue minus spending: the transfers received are added to it. Without them the account looks billions worse than it is.
budget_funds_identity_broken: The published lines do not produce the published balance, so no claim is made here that one follows from the other.
budget_funds_central: Of the transfers, {{amount}} comes from the central budget. That is part — not all — of the “transfers (net)” line in the state budget.
budget_funds_empty: NSSI has not yet published a per-fund breakdown for this year.
budget_funds_source: Source: National Social Security Institute, monthly per-fund cash-execution report (B1), as of {{asOf}}.
budget_funds_see_all: The funds and the transfer to them
budget_funds_self_over: The fund's own revenue covers {{pct}}% of its spending — it pays for itself.
budget_funds_identity_missing: One of the lines is missing from the report this site has loaded, so the account is not shown as checked.
budget_funds_plan_otheryear: ⚠️ This is a DIFFERENT year from the execution above ({{execFy}}). The ЗБДОО is passed before the year starts and the execution report arrives after it ends, so the two rarely coincide.
budget_funds_plan_intro: Separately from the execution above: this is the plan for the year — {{law}} ({{dv}}) — what the law provides, not what was executed.
budget_funds_plan_sum: Art. 1 headline: {{eur}} — sum of all funds (incl. НОИ).
budget_funds_plan_excluded: The „НОИ budget“ line ({{amount}}, {{pct}}% of the law's sum) is not shown here: it is the administration and the non-fund payments, not a fund in the way „Pensions“ is. In the same list it would be the largest entry and would read as a finding.
budget_muni_title: What the state sends each municipality
budget_muni_description: The Art. 53 transfers from the budget act — by municipality, in total and per resident.
budget_muni_intro: Municipalities do not live on local taxes alone. Much of their money arrives as a transfer from the state budget: for schools and social services they administer on the state's behalf, plus an equalisation grant and targeted funds. This is that table, municipality by municipality.
budget_muni_total_note: Ordered by total. Large municipalities naturally receive more — switch to „per resident“ to compare.
budget_muni_capita_note: Ordered per resident. The smallest municipalities come out on top, and that is not privilege. Two things explain it: some costs do not shrink with the population — 434 people still need a town hall and a school — and the equalisation grant and targeted funds exist precisely to top up municipalities with a weak tax base. For Треклянo, for instance, delegated activities are half the transfer and the other half is redistribution.
budget_muni_not_liabilities: This is what the state SENDS. What municipalities OWE — commitments entered into, expenditure liabilities and arrears — is a separate register with a different cadence and a different source; the two do not add up.
budget_muni_source: Source: Art. 53 of the State Budget Act (the per-municipality transfer table). Population is NSI Census 2021.
budget_muni_census_note: Population is from the {{year}} census, so for later years the division is approximate.
budget_muni_census_note_unknown: Population is from the latest census; its year is not published with these rows, so the division is approximate.
budget_muni_envelope_filtered_one: Sum for 1 municipality found in {{fy}} (not the national total)
budget_muni_envelope_filtered_other: Sum for {{count}} municipalities found in {{fy}} (not the national total)
budget_ipop_description: ИПОП — amounts contracted and amounts actually paid on municipal projects, municipality by municipality.
budget_ipop_intro: Under the municipal investment programme the state signs contracts with municipalities and then pays against them. The two figures diverge sharply, so they stand side by side here.
budget_ipop_rule: „Flagged“ means a contract above {{min}} on which under {{pct}}% has been paid. That is a threshold, not an assessment.
budget_ipop_flagged_claimed: Of these, {{count}} of {{total}} already have a payment submitted or awaiting settlement ({{amount}} in contracts).
budget_ipop_unavailable: Investment-programme data is not available at the moment.
budget_cap_description: The named lists of construction and capital projects — who published one, and what funds them.
budget_cap_intro: Each municipality adopts a named list of the projects it will build and repair. The lists also show where the money comes from: own revenue, a state subsidy, EU funds or borrowing.
budget_cap_coverage: This is NOT a national return. For {{fy}} it holds {{covered}} of {{total}} municipalities — {{projects}} projects. The figures below sum those municipalities only and must not be read as municipal capital spending for the country.
budget_cap_mix_h: Where the money comes from (across {{covered}} municipalities)
budget_cap_empty: No lists collected for this year.
budget_cap_unavailable: Capital-programme data is not available at the moment.
budget_cap_source: Source: the named lists of construction and capital projects annexed to each municipality's budget. Only municipalities whose lists are published in machine-readable form are collected.
budget_cap_mix_note: Only {{munis}} of {{covered}} municipalities publish a source breakdown — it covers {{amount}} of {{total}}. The percentages below are shares of that smaller sum, not of every list.
budget_cap_coverage_nodenom: This is NOT a national return. For {{fy}} it holds lists from {{covered}} municipalities — {{projects}} projects. The figures below sum those alone.
budget_hub_description: Where the state's money comes from, what it is spent on, who allocates it and what reaches the municipalities.
budget_hub_intro: A budget is one document but it answers several different questions. Each page here takes one of them and says what data it answers with.
budget_band_money_desc: How much comes in, how much goes out, how the year ended and what it goes on.
budget_band_who_desc: The spending units, the breakdowns by level, and the gap between plan and outturn.
budget_band_process_desc: The documents a budget's openness is judged by, the administration behind it, and the social-security funds.
budget_band_municipal_desc: What the state sends each municipality, and what it builds with it.
budget_hub_source: Sources: the Ministry of Finance (КФП and the budget act) via data.egov.bg, Eurostat, the social security institute, the regional development ministry and the National Audit Office. Each page states its own source and coverage.
budget_hub_metric_units_one: spending unit with a budget for {{fy}}
budget_hub_metric_units_other: spending units with a budget for {{fy}}
budget_hub_metric_deviations_one: unit with an execution report for {{fy}}
budget_hub_metric_deviations_other: units with an execution report for {{fy}}
budget_receipt_intro: Enter your gross monthly salary to see what you pay in tax and contributions over a year — and where it goes. Contributions have recipients fixed in law; only the income tax is spread across functions.
budget_receipt_your_tax: in tax and contributions per year
budget_receipt_no_income: With no salary entered, the receipt is per €100 of public spending.
budget_receipt_disclaimer: The lower block is an illustration of proportions, not a trace of money: it applies the shares public spending is divided into to your income tax. Nobody follows where your particular euros go. The shares are Eurostat's, for the whole general-government sector (state, municipalities and the social funds), so they do not add up with the state budget figures below. The contributions above are not spread this way — their recipients are fixed by the social insurance and health insurance codes. Nothing you type is stored or sent anywhere.
budget_receipt_calculator_link: The full tax calculator (self-employed, children, company) →
budget_receipt_doo: State social security — pensions, sick pay, maternity, unemployment
budget_receipt_upf: Universal pension fund — your own private account, outside government
budget_hub_muni_commitments: Separate from the state budget: municipalities have entered into commitments of {{amount}} as of {{fy}} Q{{q}}. These are the municipalities' obligations, not the state's, and a different thing from municipal debt — the two figures do not add up.
budget_maastricht_over_eurostat: above the Maastricht ceiling (3% of GDP, Eurostat basis)
budget_maastricht_under_eurostat: within the Maastricht ceiling (3% of GDP, Eurostat basis)
budget_hub_eu_contribution: Outside state budget expenditure: {{amount}} is Bulgaria's contribution to the EU budget — its own KFP line, never added to expenditure.
budget_trend_cumulative_note: КФП reporting is cumulative from the start of the year and resets each January, so the series climbs within a year and starts over.
budget_trend_projection_note: The dashed tail is a projection: the previous complete year's seasonal shape, scaled by how far ahead or behind the current year is at the same month. It is not a plan and not a commitment.
budget_trend_h: How the budget moves through the year
budget_samepoint_h: Compared with the same point in the year
budget_samepoint_intro: Every year is cut at the end of {{month}} — the point {{fy}} has reached. КФП figures accumulate from the start of the year, so comparing against previous Decembers shows a collapse every time.
budget_samepoint_note: The percentage on the right is execution against the year's statutory plan, which neutralises nominal growth. It is absent for a year running on an interim law with no adopted plan. The comparison is on MAGNITUDE: a deficit that doubled is +100%, not −100%. The median is computed from the prior years only, excluding the current one.
budget_samepoint_signmismatch: {{label}}: this year has the opposite sign to the prior ones — a magnitude comparison would mean nothing, so none is shown.
budget_donut_note: Tax revenue is broken out by tax type; the other sections stay whole. The two levels are not additive — every inner line is already inside its section.
budget_donut_note_exp: Expenditure is broken out by type; transfers and the other sections stay whole. The two levels are not additive — every inner line is already inside its section.
budget_donut_h_revenue: What the revenue is made of
budget_donut_h_expenditure: What the expenditure is made of
budget_staff_split_note: Central + territorial = the total. “Municipal” is a PART of territorial, not a third share — the three do not sum.
budget_staff_vacant_long: {{n}} of {{total}} vacant posts have been open for more than six months.
budget_staff_units_coverage: Only ministries whose report has been parsed: {{units}} for {{fy}}. Together they spend {{unitsEur}} of the state budget's {{stateEur}} — {{pct}}%.
budget_staff_units_empty: No programme-budget report has been parsed for this year.
budget_staff_chart_legend: The bars are filled posts, the solid line the approved total, the dashed line the vacancy rate (right-hand scale). The left scale does not start at zero: the establishment moves in a narrow band and every year would otherwise look identical.
